newsitem.title: USA: IMC off on possible dilution from deal.
newsitem.headline: IMC off on possible dilution from deal.

text.p: IMC Global Inc shares traded down 1-1/8 at 32-5/8 on concerns over possible earnings per share dilution from its proposed acquisition of Freeport-McMoRan Inc in a deal valued at about $800 million.
"I do think that it is dilutive in the near-term," UBS Securities analyst Ann Kohler said. "Longer term, I think very favorably of the deal."
In a statement, IMC Global said it intends to restructure its balance to make its capital structure more efficient and to "largely eliminate" any dilution.
Through the acquisition, IMC would gain full control over IMC-Agrico, its current joint venture with Freeport-McMoRan Inc. IMC-Agrico is involved in phosphate rock mining and fertilizer processing.
"I think it's certainly an appropriate move on their part, (to) consolidate the operation and streamline the decision-making process and improve their response time," Kohler said.
She added there are some cost-saving opportunities to be reaped in the deal.

But Lehman Bros analyst Peter Ward cautioned that the cost savings could be limited since the acquisition eliminates mostly holding company and joint venture structures and does not combine production operations.
Ward added that he believes the deal will be roughly neutral to earnings in the short-term.
Freeport-McMoRan Inc shares rose 4-3/16 to 30-11/16 on the deal.
